configuration_provenance.old_profile: three messages, fixed complete source prefix plus finite task; read timeout 180s, total 900s; maximum_attempts=6 includes first attempt; no arbitrary semantic retries or stitching partial streams

evidence_and_source_boundary: An existing single profile contained 300 business Java samples and 137 native samples. JSON constructor and document validation inclusive counts were 63 and 61; inclusive counts overlap and are not invocations, CPU seconds or attribution of the full phase wall.

The source had a strict UTF-8 decoder whose returned character buffer was discarded before a byte parser decoded again. This is a real source-level duplicate, not proof that replacing the parser preserves its accepted or rejected language.
Exact Jackson-core 2.21.7 software jar and same-version official source archive were pinned. This is not a reproducible source-to-jar receipt or a new proof of the current live loader mapping.

The old archive token path already performed cache lookup and complete content comparison before constructing a new JSON value. That proposed reorder was closed without a patch; physical reads and qualification remained intact.

rejected_trial.scope: Reuse a strict-decoder-owned character buffer for selected material before the original byte parser fallback.
rejected_trial.model_implementation: Some executable text was used in the private trial; owner added a missing import and a checked IOException fallback. The entire resulting trial was later rejected and never formally adopted.
rejected_trial.model_counter: Whole proof rejected: it used a false UTF-8 BOM premise and an unrelated factory mismatch. It did not establish the real symbol-table failure difference.
rejected_trial.model_test: Whole executable proposal rejected for invalid NUL-padded documents, contradictory assertions, wrong escaped-name assumptions and an admitted size violation; the owner wrote the four-method trial test.
rejected_trial.software: First one-TU compile, new test compile and four selected methods passed. Those four passes are trial evidence only and are not counted as ASCII or tree-buffer passes.
rejected_trial.remaining_real_counterexample: The byte parser uses ByteQuads while the character parser uses Chars canonicalization. Their collision overflow policy and byte-versus-character name bounds differ even for otherwise valid material.
rejected_trial.bounded_owner_source_proof: A deterministic family of 300 unique 40-byte ASCII names permutes seven four-byte suffix chunks after fixed prefix quads. The byte long-name hash combines those suffix chunks by an order-independent sum, giving the same hash for every seed by source algebra. A fresh default byte table exhausts its spill capacity before all 300, whereas the character table needs more than 300 insertions to trigger its repeated-chain failure. This was a source/Python construction, not an executed Java parser test, observed live seed or universal loaded-binary proof.

accepted_ascii_byte_lane.principle: Scan the private defensive byte clone. If every byte is nonnegative, every byte is ASCII and therefore valid UTF-8, including NUL. Only the separate strict UTF-8 decoder can be omitted. Any negative byte executes the entire original strict decoder; the original byte parser always runs and retains encoding autodetection, canonicalizer, grammar, number, duplicate, Unicode and trailing checks.
accepted_ascii_byte_lane.production_and_test: Owner authored the one production literal and a new public two-method test. Implementation/counter/test model requests for this algorithm exhausted configured transport attempts with zero headers and zero content, so there was no semantic model answer to adopt.
accepted_ascii_byte_lane.new_test_scope: ASCII controls, DEL, NUL-based original encoding autodetection, valid non-ASCII, first and late invalid/overlong/surrogate UTF-8, and decoder-before-parser failure order. Two distinct methods passed; no old trial methods were run.

formal_production.eol: LF projection preserving other source text

bounded_tree_character_lane.principle: This consumer already used the character parser through a String. The exact library String overload takes its fixed character-buffer route only at at most 32768 characters; the larger-input StringReader route remains unchanged. Reuse the private decoder-owned buffer only in that same short route, with the same character canonicalizer and tree visitor. Do not infer safety from the rejected byte-to-character trial.
bounded_tree_character_lane.resource_revision: After parser acquisition and before tree construction, explicitly clear the decoder local. The parser already owns its short input or the independent String-based reader. This shortens interpreter-local reachability; it is not a heap-peak, OOM, GC or throughput guarantee.
bounded_tree_character_lane.model_results: A broad model source answer was rejected for false changed-UTF8 and mutable-buffer premises. The actual-delta counter and witness roles ended in transport exhaustion with no content. Owner authored the narrow source and two-method public test.
bounded_tree_character_lane.test_scope: Independent mutable trees, integer and decimal token fidelity, preserved legacy lone-surrogate acceptance, input isolation, 32768/32769 boundaries, strict UTF-8, depth and original character error offsets. The earlier source tuple passed two new distinct methods.
bounded_tree_character_lane.why_no_GC_mirror_test: The final delta is a local-reference clear after parser acquisition, with no subsequent read of that local by the unchanged visitor. Its structural source proof and strict compile are recorded separately from prior dynamic tests.
bounded_tree_character_lane.current_formal_baseline_note: The writer discovered that its formal baseline already had a broader buffer route, while this investigation used the old String source. Only the overlapping owned parser block is being reconciled; earlier tests are not represented as a comparison against that different formal baseline.
bounded_tree_character_lane.support_boundary: Existing dependency classes were qualified only for their used binary APIs; their whole source-to-class receipts and live mapping remain unknown.

one_parent_http_ledger.initial_roles: Three completed STOP/valid-JSON responses, one attempt each. Private implementation was partially used only in the later rejected trial; counter and test executable proposals were rejected.
one_parent_http_ledger.eight_remaining_source_roles: Eight genuine unfinished source questions used fourteen actual attempts; six initial partial streams were discarded and their configured transport retries completed. No production code from these roles was adopted.
one_parent_http_ledger.six_followup_roles: Six genuine algorithm/counter/witness tasks used six attempts each, with zero headers and zero content. These are transport failures, not malformed or semantically bad model answers.
one_parent_http_ledger.not_new_denominators: Earlier trial four passes, ASCII two passes and earlier tree two passes are three separate software scopes; component notes do not repeat their request costs. No old green source or test methods were rerun to enlarge counts.

cost_and_limits.wall_includes: Rejected work, preparation, source review, model waits and retries, resource scheduling and first software checks; overlapping subwindows must not be added as independent elapsed time.
cost_and_limits.preparation_errors: One draft prefix was corrected before POST, one inline preparation command had a quoting SyntaxError before mutation, and one later small metadata read used the wrong subdirectory. These are owner preparation costs, not model or software failures.
